newsitem.title: USA: US consumer confidence index lower in July.
newsitem.headline: US consumer confidence index lower in July.

text.p: The index of U.S. consumer confidence fell to 126.5 in July, down more than three points from June's revised 129.9, the Conference Board said Tuesday.
The expectations component of the index, which has proven to be a key measure of future business activity, fell to 107.6 in July from a revised 111.7 in June.
The Present Situations Index fell to 154.8 in July from 157.1 in June.

"Despite the slight decline in consumer confidence this month, both the Present Situation and Expectation Indexes are running at historically high levels," said Lynn Franco, associate director of the Conference Board's Consumer Research Center. "While consumer confidence is subject to fluctuations, latest readings continue to signal healthy economic growth ahead."
